Requiring a      minimum tick displacement means the median only reacts to swaps      that actually pushed the pool to a new price level \u2014 not to      repeated pokes at essentially the same price, which is exactly the      kind of cheap, repeatable action an attacker would use to drag the      median toward a favorable value. The required displacement is not      a flat constant \u2014 it is scaled by the pool's current liquidity      depth in `requiredMovement`, because the same tick move means very      different things in a deep pool vs. a shallow one.      Operates directly on the caller's storage via a `storage` struct      reference (the same pattern OpenZeppelin uses for EnumerableSet /      Checkpoints).","kind":"dev","methods":{},"stateVariables":{"BASE_TICK_THRESHOLD":{"details":"This is the value used when the pool's liquidity sits exactly      at `REFERENCE_LIQUIDITY`; see `requiredMovement` for how it's      scaled up/down for other liquidity levels."},"MAX_TICK_THRESHOLD":{"details":"Without it, an extremely deep pool could push the requirement      to 0 (median updates on every single swap, defeating the whole      point of gating it)."},"MIN_TICK_THRESHOLD":{"details":"Without it, a near-zero-liquidity pool could push the      requirement to an absurdly large value (median effectively      frozen forever)."},"REFERENCE_LIQUIDITY":{"details":"Pools deeper than this need a SMALLER tick move to trigger an      update (moving the tick there took a large, expensive trade,      so it's already a meaningful signal). Pools shallower than      this need a LARGER tick move (a tiny trade can swing a thin      pool's tick a lot, so that movement alone proves little and is      cheap to manufacture).
